questions.question: What is the best protection for a motorcycle rider?

options.text: Keep space between your motorcycle and other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep space between your motorcycle and other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Your best protection against crashes is to keep distance from other vehicles. Space gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake. Good gear is also important when riding.

questions.question: How much stopping power does a motorcycle's front brake provide?
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's front brake is stronger than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: What blood alcohol concentration (BAC) level means a person is legally intoxicated?
questions.explanation: A person age 21 or older with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher is legally intoxicated. It is illegal and dangerous to drive any vehicle while intoxicated.

questions.question: What is the minimum following distance when riding a motorcycle at night?
questions.explanation: Darkness makes it harder to see and judge distances. Keep at least three seconds of distance behind other vehicles at night. You need extra time to notice when a vehicle stops and to slow down or stop.

questions.question: How do you stop a motorcycle with maximum braking power in a straight line?

options.text: Use the rear brake and downshift.

questions.explanation: Maximum stopping power comes from using both the front and rear brakes fully without locking either wheel. Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: What does a linked braking system do?

options.text: It connects the front and rear brakes so both work when you use either brake.
It connects the front brake to the gear shifter and applies the brake when downshifting.
It connects the rear brake to a foot control.
It connects the rear brake to a switch on the handlebar.

questions.correctAnswerText: It connects the front and rear brakes so both work when you use either brake.
questions.explanation: A linked braking system connects the front and rear brakes together. When you use either brake lever, both brakes get pressure. Check your owner's manual for details about your motorcycle's braking system.

questions.question: What color vest or jacket helps you be seen best while riding?
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors to be more visible while riding. Bright orange, yellow, red, or green work best. Avoid dark or dull colors.

questions.question: Where should you place heavier cargo on a motorcycle?

options.text: In front of the tank bag
Near the front with lighter items
Avoid placing items over the rear axle

questions.correctAnswerText: In front of the tank bag
questions.explanation: Place heavier items in front of the tank bag. Put the load over or in front of the rear axle. Putting weight behind the rear axle can affect your control.

questions.question: What is found in the center of a traffic lane?

options.text: Debris and oil drippings from vehicles
The safest place for motorcycle riders to travel
Where drivers are least likely to see a motorcycle

questions.correctAnswerText: Debris and oil drippings from vehicles
questions.explanation: Debris and oil drippings collect in the center of a lane. You may also find utility hole covers and other hazards there.

questions.question: When is it most important to flash your brake light?

options.text: When you need to slow down suddenly
When there is a stop sign ahead
When your signals do not work

questions.correctAnswerText: When you need to slow down suddenly
questions.explanation: A motorcycle has only one brake light, which is less noticeable than a car's two larger brake lights. Flashing your brake light helps others notice it, especially when you slow down faster than expected.

questions.question: When riding in fog, what should you do?

options.text: Switch between low and high beams.

questions.explanation: Use your low beam headlight in fog. Do not use high beams when other vehicles are nearby.

questions.question: How many paths of travel does each traffic lane offer a motorcyclist?
questions.explanation: Each traffic lane has three paths: the left side, center, and right side of the lane.

questions.question: Why should you not move to the far side of your lane when being passed?

options.text: It discourages the passing driver from cutting into your lane too early.
It encourages the passing driver to cut into your lane too early.
It encourages the passing driver to complete the pass quickly.
It encourages other drivers to pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It encourages the passing driver to cut into your lane too early.
questions.explanation: Moving to the far side of your lane is dangerous. It may cause the passing driver to return to your lane before it is safe. Stay in the center of your lane when being passed.

questions.question: What is the best lane position for a motorcycle rider?

options.text: The left side of the lane
The right side of the lane
There is no single best lane position for all situations.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is no single best lane position for all situations.
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position based on your current riding conditions. This helps you maintain safe distance from other vehicles and stay visible to other drivers.

questions.question: Is a helmet required for passengers?

options.text: Yes, but only if the operator has had their license less than two years.

questions.explanation: Motorcycle operators and passengers under 18, and riders with a permit, must wear approved helmets. All riders should wear helmets every time they ride.

questions.question: When riding in traffic, how should a motorcycle operator position themselves in the lane?

options.text: Always ride in the same part of the lane.
Change lane position based on riding conditions.
Always ride in the center of the lane.
Always ride on the left side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lane position based on riding conditions.
questions.explanation: There is no single best lane position. Change your position based on road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: Which of these should NOT be true about a helmet?

options.text: It does not meet U.S. DOT standards.
It was worn in an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: It was worn in an accident.
questions.explanation: A good helmet must meet DOT standards, fit snugly, and have no obvious defects. If a helmet was worn during a crash, replace it.

questions.question: When riding in a group, what should riders do?

options.text: Spread out so the group is easier to see.
Stay close together so the group is easier to see.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay close together so the group is easier to see.
questions.explanation: Stay close together as a group while keeping safe distance around each rider. This makes the group easier to see and keeps riders from getting separated. Do not pair up because it does not allow enough room to maneuver.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When you can see the roadway through vehicles ahead.
When the weather is pleasant and clear.

questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when conditions require longer stopping distances, such as poor weather, at night, when you cannot see through the vehicle ahead, or when traffic is heavy. A two-second distance is generally adequate in normal conditions.

questions.question: Why should motorcycle riders not rely only on mirrors?

options.text: Motorcycle mirrors are too small to see much.
Motorcycles have blind spots, just like cars.
Mirrors take your eyes off the road ahead and should not be used.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles have blind spots, just like cars.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any vehicle. You cannot rely only on mirrors to see what is behind you. Check over your shoulder frequently.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a benefit of riding in a close group?

options.text: It uses minimal space on the highway.
The group is easy to see.
The group is unlikely to get separated.
A close group reaches the destination faster than a spread-out group.

questions.correctAnswerText: A close group reaches the destination faster than a spread-out group.
questions.explanation: Riding in a close group is better than riding spread out because it takes up less road space, is easier to see, and reduces the chance of riders getting separated at traffic lights and during passes.

questions.question: When riding in curves, turning, or entering a highway, the best group formation is:
questions.explanation: Staggered formation is usually best for group riding. However, use single-file when riding through curves, making turns, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.explanation: Signs that show road rules, such as speed limits, are usually rectangular with white backgrounds and black lettering. You must follow all rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: A passenger should never:
questions.explanation: In South Carolina, passengers under 21 must wear a helmet and eye protection. All riders should wear helmets and eye protection. Passengers should avoid loose clothing that might catch on the motorcycle and must always lean with the driver when turning. Passengers should never ride sidesaddle.

questions.question: A motorcyclist can discourage other vehicles from lane sharing by:

options.text: Riding on the left side of the lane.
Riding in the center of the lane.
Making angry looks at other drivers.
Riding in a zigzag pattern across the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riding in the center of the lane.
questions.explanation: To prevent other drivers from trying to squeeze into your lane, ride in the center of the lane.

questions.question: A proper lane position should do all of the following, EXCEPT:

options.text: Increase your ability to see and be seen.
Show your intentions to other drivers.

questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see others and be seen. It keeps you away from wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. A good lane position also discourages other drivers from sharing your lane and gives you an escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: If a friend has been drinking and wants to drive, which should you NOT do?

options.text: Get other friends to talk them out of driving.
Tell them to use less-crowded roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell them to use less-crowded roads.
questions.explanation: To prevent drunk driving, you can arrange other transportation, involve them in activities to slow their drinking, find excuses to keep them from leaving before they sober up, and get other friends to help stop them.

questions.question: When following a car, the best lane position is usually:
questions.explanation: When riding behind a car, ride in the center of the lane so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror. Drivers check rearview mirrors much more often than side mirrors, which increases your chances of being seen.

questions.question: When exiting a highway in a group, which formation should you use?
questions.explanation: Staggered formation is usually best for group riding. Switch to single-file when riding through curves, making turns, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: You will ______ hear a tire going flat.
questions.explanation: You will rarely hear a tire going flat on a motorcycle. Tire failure is usually noticed by a change in how the motorcycle handles.
